# AwsAuth, detected

`runbooks test` signs these blocks in against the fake AWS provider (`blocks/aws-auth/fake.ts`), which knows the secret key `fake-aws-secret-0001`.

`aws` looks in the environment, and pins nothing, so the person confirms the login it finds.

<AwsAuth id="aws" title="Sign in to AWS" description="Use the **staging** keys." />

`prod` reads only the `PROD_` variables, and pins its account and role, so a login that reaches them needs no confirmation.

<AwsAuth
  id="prod"
  detectCredentials={[{ env: { prefix: "PROD_" } }]}
  ssoAccountId="111111111111"
  ssoRoleName="Admin"
/>

`deploy` gets `aws`'s keys through `envFrom`, and only through it.

<Command
  id="deploy"
  envFrom={["aws"]}
  command={`test "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" = fake-aws-secret-0001 || exit 7`}
/>
